title: A/B rollout hypothesis log and ops patterns (working)
body:
Purpose

This is a working doc for documenting the hypothesis-driven A/B and canary rollouts we run across console features and runtime routing changes. The goal: a compact, repeatable checklist and hypothesis log that helps cross-functional teams (product, eng, SRE, data, QA, CS) run predictable experiments and rapid, safe rollouts.

Scope
- Applies to: UI/Console behavioral changes, model routing changes (model pair rollouts, fallback policies), traffic-splitting at the edge, and server-side feature flags that can affect latency/cost/quality.
- Not covered here: long-running feature branches, major infra migrations (separate infra-retire playbook).

Quick Summary / TL;DR (for on-call + PM)
- Always bake a single measurable hypothesis (what metric improves and what risk we accept).
- Use three-tier slices: small internal slice (0.5-2%), trusted customers (2-10%), broad production (10->100%).
- Define clear safety/abort gates (latency SLO breach, error-rate spike, quality delta).
- Instrument: request-id tracing, model-version tag, cohort id, prompt hash (where applicable).
- Post-rollout: run the evaluation checklist within 48 hours, store artifacts in the experiment ticket, and mark the hypothesis PASS/FAIL.

Hypothesis template (one line to copy into ticket)
- Hypothesis: "If we route X% of eligible traffic to model v2 + prefix-cache, we will reduce 95th p99 generation latency by >= 15ms and improve conversion for feature Y by +2% without increasing error-rate above 0.5%."
- Primary metric (signal): p95 generation latency (route:model=v2).
- Secondary metric (biz): conversion rate on CTA Y (events / eligible requests).
- Safety metric (guardrail): 5xx rate and immediate model fallback errors (per-route error-rate).

Experiment logging: required fields for the experiment ticket
- Hypothesis text (see above).
- Experiment owner (single person).
- Start date / expected rollout runway.
- Traffic partition plan (table).
- Data owner (who will own evaluation queries).
- Monitoring dashboards / baseline links.
- Abort criteria (numeric thresholds).
- Rollback plan and hotfix contact list.

Traffic partition patterns (recommended)
- Canary micro: 0.5% randomly sampled internal employees (via allowlist or cookie). Purpose: smoke test.
- Canary narrow: 2-5% trusted customers (customer segments with success history). Purpose: early signal with real customers.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 24-72 hours depending on risk.
- Deterministic cohorts: for UX experiments that need consistent experience, pin cohorts using customer-id hashing.

Slice mapping cheat-sheet (quick)
- Latency-sensitive slices: heavy read routes + low TTL caching (monitor p95/p99).
- Quality-sensitive slices: chat and completion endpoints with brand-sensitive content (monitor human evals + automated quality score).
- Cost-sensitive slices: high-volume internal API vs. low-volume interactive UI.

Monitoring checklist (pre-roll & during)
- Create an experiment dashboard with: throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end and server-only), 5xx/4xx rates, model-specific error categories, token-cost delta, business conversion metric, and sample outputs stream for manual review.
- Add anomaly detection alerts for sudden delta > 20% on safety metrics or sustained latency breach > 10% above SLO.
- Ensure synthetic traffic runs against the canary route every 5 minutes (sanity test).
- Verify logs contain model_version, experiment_id, cohort_id, route_tag.

Abort and rollback rules (conservative default)
- Immediate abort if: error-rate for the variant > 0.5 percentage points above baseline for 5 consecutive minutes and absolute 5xx rate > 0.2%.
- Immediate rollback if: p99 latency degrades by > 30% vs baseline sustained for 15 minutes.
- Conditional pause (manual review) if: business metric change beyond expected CI but safety metrics okay.
- Communications: trigger #rollouts Slack channel, page SRE on-call if the abort threshold is hit.

Operational play patterns (ops recipes)
- Fast-fail canary: 0.5% for 30m -> analyze; if no regressions, ramp to 5% for 1h; if clean, publish to 20% -> 100% in steps.
- Side-by-side shadowing: run v2 in shadow on 10% of traffic (no production effect) for 24–72h to collect quality metrics before any live routing.
- Feature-flag Bisection: if a broad rollout causes regression, use binary traffic split to find the inflection point (50/50 -> 25/75 -> 12.5/87.5).

Data & evaluation (who does what)
- Data analyst: implement experiment SQL queries, compute confidence intervals, and flag statistically significant differences.
- Product: interpret biz impact and approve progression.
- Eng: validate instrumentation, own rollback automation, and fix hot path.
- QA/Applied ML: manual spot-checks for quality and hallucination cases; sample N=50 outputs per slice per day for median checks.

Manual review checklist for sampled outputs
- Is output on-topic and relevant? (yes/no)
- Any unsafe or PII leaks? (yes/no)
- Obvious hallucination or factually incorrect (scale 1–5).
- Flag and link the sample to the incident tracker if severity > 3.

Experiment artifact checklist (what to store)
- Dashboard permalink + baseline snapshot.
- Raw sample outputs (anonymized) + sampling seed.
- SQL and code used for evaluation.
- Final verdict and short rationale (pass/fail/undecided).

Ceremonies and timeline (recommended cadence)
- Pre-launch sync (30 min): owners across product, eng, data, SRE, QA confirm instrumentation and rollforward/back plans.
- T-minus 0 (launch): announce on #rollouts and update ticket status.
- T+4h: quick health check (engineering).
- T+24h: interim analysis (data + product).
- T+72h or when stable: final decision and comment summary.

Open questions / TODOs
- Autoscaling interactions: do we need separate autoscale rules for canary pools? (TODO: infra proposal).
- Cost throttles: add token-cost per-route alert to avoid runaway spend.
- Improve sample output collection pipeline to redact PII automatically.

Appendix: example abort thresholds (copy into ticket)
- p99 latency increase > 30ms and relative +20% vs baseline for 15m -> PAUSE.
- end-to-end error-rate delta > 0.5pp sustained 5m -> ABORT.
- token cost per request increase > 40% -> REVIEW.

Notes to self / fragments (working)
- Consider a lightweight experiment registry service that stores hypothesis metadata, experiment lifecycle, and artifact links (low priority).
- Need a one-click rollback button in Console for model routing changes (eng + console TODO).

Contact list (quick)
- Product lead: Sophie Chen (owner)
- Eng lead: Jon Park
- SRE on-call: PagerDuty roster (use #rollouts for escalation)
- Data analyst: Elena Morales

If you're editing this doc: keep it short, prefer copyable templates, and add new experiment logs as numbered entries under a future "experiment-log" file.

----
Change history (small)
- 2024-09-18: initial draft (Sophie).
- 2024-10-22: added sample outputs checklist and abort thresholds (Ravi).
- 2024-12-03: tightened latency abort rule and added synthetic traffic requirement (Maya).
